spark.byteSummary:
Master relational modeling, B+Tree indexes, MVCC isolation, query execution plans, and scaling patterns for PostgreSQL and MySQL.

A B+Tree keeps keys sorted in balanced disk pages (typically 8–16 KB), turning O(N) full table scans into O(log N) 3–4 page reads.

Strong SQL engineering combines normalized data modeling, composite index ordering, and safe schema evolution.

learningJourney.title: B+Tree indexes, leftmost prefix & covering indexes
learningJourney.explanation: A [B+Tree](/concept/btree-vs-lsmtree) keeps keys sorted in balanced disk pages (typically 8–16 KB), turning O(N) full table scans into O(log N) 3–4 page reads.

ideas.title: Leftmost Prefix Rule
ideas.description: An index on `(tenant_id, created_at)` accelerates `WHERE tenant_id = ?` and `(tenant_id, created_at > ?)`, but NOT `WHERE created_at > ?` alone.

ideas.title: Covering Index (INCLUDE)
ideas.description: Including non-key columns in the leaf pages enables Index-Only Scans without fetching heap pages.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```sql
-- Composite + covering index for multi-tenant timeline queries (PostgreSQL)
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_tenant_created
ON orders (tenant_id, created_at DESC) INCLUDE (status, total_cents);
```

learningJourney.title: MVCC, vacuuming, and zero-downtime DDL

tabbedExplorer.name: MVCC & Locks
tabbedExplorer.title: Snapshot Isolation vs. Explicit Row Locking
tabbedExplorer.desc: Readers never block writers in MVCC, but concurrent read-modify-write invariants still require `FOR UPDATE` or `SERIALIZABLE`.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Always acquire row locks in deterministic sorted ID order to prevent deadlocks.

tabbedExplorer.name: Expand & Contract
tabbedExplorer.title: Zero-Downtime Schema Migrations
tabbedExplorer.desc: Add nullable columns / `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, dual-write, backfill in batches, then drop old columns.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Always set `lock_timeout` on DDL so a waiting `ALTER TABLE` doesn't queue up all app reads/writes.
tabbedExplorer.use: Production migrations on live multi-million-row tables.

learningJourney.title: Read replicas, connection pooling & partitioning
learningJourney.explanation: Scale connections with PgBouncer, offload analytics to replicas, and partition massive time-ordered tables.

qaDetails.summary: Why does `OFFSET 500000 LIMIT 20` get slower on later pages?
qaDetails.body: The database must still fetch and sort 500,020 rows before discarding the first 500,000. Keyset (cursor) pagination `WHERE (created_at, id) < (?, ?)` uses the B+Tree index in O(log N).

qaDetails.summary: Why do high-connection microservices need PgBouncer / connection pooling?
qaDetails.body: Each Postgres connection spawns a backend OS process (~5–10MB RAM + context switching). Pooling multiplexes thousands of app requests onto dozens of active DB connections.

knowledgeCheck.question: A table has a composite index on `(tenant_id, status, created_at)`. Which query CANNOT efficiently use this B+Tree index?

options.feedback: Uses the first two leading columns of the index.
Correct! Skipping the leftmost column `tenant_id` violates the B+Tree leftmost prefix rule.

options.text: C. WHERE tenant_id = 5 ORDER BY status
options.feedback: Uses `tenant_id` for lookup and `status` in index order.

tipsAndTricks: Put equality columns before range columns in composite B+Tree indexes: `(tenant_id, created_at)` beats `(created_at, tenant_id)` for per-tenant feeds.
Replace `OFFSET` pagination with cursor/keyset pagination on indexed columns.
Always run `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` and set `lock_timeout` in migrations to prevent table-wide stalls.
finalSummaryEyebrow: The idea to keep with you
finalSummaryTitle: Index for selectivity, keep transactions short, and read EXPLAIN ANALYZE before guessing.
